name: Drawing Space Separation (DSS)
definition: A volumetric display technique that separates the space where graphics are drawn (drawing space) from the space users view (viewing space) using a re-projection system. This allows the drawing space to be filled with materials (e.g., xenon gas) that lower the energy threshold for voxel generation without creating a physical barrier between the user and the graphics, and enables color extraction mechanisms (e.g., LC filters) within the drawing space.
